stacks.title: Evidence preservation & web history
stacks.summary: Save a page before it changes, find its older versions, and record what a server showed, each with a date.

steps.do: Save the page first. Save Page Now makes a dated copy with a permanent link, even if the page later changes or disappears. Then open its calendar of older copies to see when something appeared or changed.
For context beyond web pages: the wider Internet Archive holds books, newspapers, audio, video and software from the same period.
If a server is part of the story, Shodan's records show what it exposed on a given date. Note that date: a record can be stale.

notes: Keep the date and the archive link with every copy you save, and say plainly which links you couldn't confirm.
archive.ph (archive.today) is left out on purpose: in 2026 some of its copies were found altered. See its card.

source.label: Adapted from OSINT4ALL's Evidence Preservation and Historical Web Stack

comparisons.title: Shodan, Censys or SecurityTrails?
comparisons.question: Looking up a server, an IP address or a domain
comparisons.framing: Built from each tool's own pages and documentation, not a hands-on accuracy test. Read each tool's limit before trusting a result.

pick.when: you need to know which services were seen on a specific server or IP address.
your lead is a certificate, or you want to know what answers at a hostname.
you need to know how a domain's DNS records changed over time.

steps: Write down exactly which domain, server or organization you are allowed to look into.
Check DNS and domain history first, keeping current records apart from old ones.
Look up host, service and certificate records, and note the date on each one.
Confirm anything important with a second source, such as crt.sh for certificates.
Keep a short record of every source, and say plainly which links you couldn't confirm.
notes: These tools show what others have already indexed. Scanning or testing a system yourself needs its owner's permission.
A free web search is not the same as API access. Check query and export limits before planning bulk work.

source.label: Adapted from OSINT4ALL's comparison of the same three tools
